acceptedLaws: Provider Protocol Continuation is not Agent cognition: Provider-required opaque continuation bytes may be retained and reprojected to the bound Adapter without becoming model-visible semantic messages.
Provider continuation authority comes from an exact prior Provider Tool result and exact completed-Provider lineage, not from caller-supplied message shape.

Continuation recovery follows existing privacy authority: metadata-only Runs do not secretly retain opaque Provider content; exact crash/reopen recovery requires content retention already authorized by the Run Contract.
Stable protocol/tool prefixes plus trailing per-turn dynamic authority survived independent DeepSeek and Gemini locality experiments, while concrete wire layout remains Provider-specific.
Exact claim/dispatch/UNKNOWN semantics are justified where the external world lacks strong idempotency/result lookup; they are not a universal replacement for checkpoint replay.

effectSemantics.finding: Without external idempotency, checkpoint replay duplicated effects in response-loss, post-effect crash and concurrent-entry controls while exact lifecycle duplicated none and retained UNKNOWN where physical outcome could not be proved; with idempotency plus result lookup the approaches can converge.

navigation.finding: Both extended controls exact-read the correct concurrency file but neither lawfully finalized in the bounded frontier; map advantage was not established.

observability.afterRecover: 3/3 chose reconcile-external-state and 0/3 allowed Provider redispatch.
observability.beforeRecover: 3/3 chose recover and 0/3 allowed Provider redispatch.
observability.finding: Existing inspect -> recover -> reconcile operator surface was sufficient for a blind Agent on a real durable Provider UNKNOWN.

publicSurface.nonClaim: Name-only symbol-selection controls were confusing, but they did not model the documented product surface and therefore did not earn deletion of public exports.
publicSurface.recommendedPath: 4/4 blind current-doc integrations selected HarnessAgentRun without advanced composition.

nonClaims: Harness does not interpret Gemini thought-signature semantics or expose those bytes as Agent reasoning.
No built-in Gemini Adapter is added by this acceptance.
Provider continuation is not a Memory/RAG channel and cannot be injected by caller message content.
Cross-Provider stable-prefix evidence does not define Provider internal KV-cache implementation or a universal cache-hit threshold.
AST repository maps remain optional navigation instruments, not source truth or Harness authority.

boundaries: AgentTurnResult may carry one Tool-result continuation bound to adapter, source turn and source model call.
AgentTurnRequest carries ordered Provider continuations separately from model-visible messages.
AgentTurnProjector strips Harness-reserved continuation metadata from semantic messages.
SQLite continuity independently reconstructs and verifies continuation authority before Provider claim.
initial run messages and resume additional messages cannot inject Harness-reserved continuation metadata.

scope: Five-frontier Harness cross-validation round. Public-surface minimality, effect semantics, repository navigation and operator observability were required to beat simpler controls before productization; only a second native Provider exposed an otherwise inexpressible state transition and earned source change.

cacheLocality.nonClaim: Observed cache realization is Provider-controlled and is not a fixed release threshold.

signatureFalsifier.interpretation: A semantic Tool call plus raw-response digest is insufficient for this Provider protocol; exact opaque continuation must survive into the next request.
